cases.description: A well‑formed JSON document that satisfies the schema (e.g., required property "name" of type string) should produce an empty ValidationMessage set.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a message about missing required property "name"
cases.description: JSON is syntactically correct but violates the schema (required property missing). The method should return a set with at least one ValidationMessage describing the violation.
An empty string cannot be deserialized into a JsonNode; the implementation is expected to throw an IllegalArgumentException (or a subclass) indicating that the input is empty or invalid.
Passing a null reference for the input string should result in a NullPointerException before any deserialization attempt.
Malformed JSON (missing quotes around property name) should cause the underlying Jackson parser to fail, which the validate method propagates as a parsing exception.
A correctly formatted YAML document that satisfies the same schema should be deserialized and validated without errors when InputFormat.YAML is specified.

cases.expected: non‑empty set containing a type‑mismatch message for property "age"
cases.description: YAML document is syntactically valid but violates the schema because "age" is not an integer as required; validation should return a message describing the type error.
Providing JSON content while declaring the format as YAML should cause the YAML parser to fail, resulting in a parsing exception.
A string containing only whitespace is not a valid JSON document; the method should reject it with an IllegalArgumentException.
JSON that contains additional properties not defined in the schema should still pass validation when "additionalProperties" is allowed (default behavior).
The InputFormat argument is null. The method should fail fast with a NullPointerException before attempting deserialization.
The input string contains malformed percent‑encoding. If the implementation URL‑decodes the string during deserialization, it should raise an UnsupportedEncodingException.
An InputFormat value that is not supported by the deserializer (e.g., a hypothetical UNKNOWN constant) should cause the method to reject the request with an IllegalArgumentException.
